extension.description: A Kodi metadata scraper for TV shows, backed by your self-hosted Chronicle server. Unlike a normal scraper, it never talks to TheTVDB or any other upstream source directly -- it only ever asks Chronicle, which resolves-and-creates the item through whichever metadata providers you've already configured there, so Kodi always ends up seeing exactly what Chronicle itself would show for that title -- seasons and episodes, multi-source ratings, and all. Movies are a separate sibling addon, script.chronicle.scraper.movie -- install both if you track both. They have to be separate addons: Kodi resolves which script to run for a scrape by addon id alone, not by which extension point (movies vs tvshows) triggered the call, so one addon declaring both would silently run the wrong script for TV every time. Has its own "Connect to Chronicle" QR/PIN flow and its own API key, independent of the Movies addon -- open the addon (or its Settings) to connect. "Rebuild local NFOs from Chronicle" and the corner status indicator live in the Movies addon and cover both movies and TV shows together; this addon doesn't duplicate them.
extension.news: v1.1.1 - "Connect to Chronicle" now confirms the Chronicle URL directly (a text prompt, pre-filled with whatever's currently saved) instead of trusting chronicle_url on disk. Confirmed live: switching URLs in Settings and immediately clicking "Connect to Chronicle" (the action button lives inside that same still-open Settings dialog) built the QR code against the OLD URL -- a just-typed text field's value isn't guaranteed to be flushed to settings.xml before Kodi launches the RunScript action as a brand new process, so the fresh process could read stale data even though the new value was visibly still sitting in the field. This also fixes the fresh-install case: opening the addon for the first time now prompts for the URL right in the Connect flow instead of requiring a value to already be saved before Connect can do anything with it. v1.1.0 - This addon now shows up as a launchable entry in the Kodi add-on browser and has its own "Connect to Chronicle" QR/PIN flow -- previously it only ever exposed the xbmc.metadata.scraper.tvshows hook, with no script entry point at all, so connecting it meant manually copying the URL and API key over from Chronicle Scraper (Movies)'s settings. New default.py (own menu: Test Connection / Connect to Chronicle / Open Settings -- deliberately not duplicating Movies' NFO-rebuild menu entry, see that file's own docstring), lib/device_auth.py and lib/qr_dialog.py ported from the Movies addon, resources/qr_panel.png copied over. api_key is now a hidden setting set by the QR flow rather than a plain text field you paste into by hand, matching the Movies addon's UX. Also: device_auth.py's "Could not contact the Chronicle server" dialog now shows the actual reason (empty URL, DNS failure, connection refused, timeout, HTTP error, etc.) instead of the same generic text for every failure. v1.0.1 - Three fixes, all found in code review: (1) lib/legacy_nfo.py's stash directory was still under special://profile/addon_data/{addon_id}/ in this addon's copy, scoped to this addon's own id -- meaning a TV show's stashed legacy-NFO data (harvested by this addon's delete step) could never be found by the re-scrape that consumes it, since that re-scrape also runs from this same addon's process but the path itself was never actually reachable in the intended cross-addon case. Now stashes under special://temp/chronicle_scraper/, matching rebuild_state.py and activity_tracker.py. (2) settings.xml had an invalid XML comment (a literal "--" inside the comment body, which XML never allows outside the opening/closing delimiters) -- replaced with an em dash. (3) strings.po's #32092 help text had unescaped literal quote marks inside its msgid, breaking that string's parsing -- now escaped to match the convention used everywhere else in this file. v1.0.0 - Split out of script.chronicle.scraper (now script.chronicle.scraper.movie) as its own addon, so Kodi can actually invoke the TV scraper -- see that addon's v3.0.0 changelog entry for the full root-cause explanation. Same code as tvshow_scraper.py always had (the v2.13.2 endOfDirectory fix and the v2.13.3 rebuild-pass-only NFO gating), just finally reachable.
